questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over confirming the file's save location and the opportunity to immediately inspect its contents.

questions.question: Does the browser's download UI show a security warning requiring you to explicitly click 'Keep'?
questions.why: Browsers sometimes flag files with a visual warning in the downloads bar that pauses the download until manually approved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that the file is held in a suspended state by the browser's security filter.

children.label: Choose the file type at the point of download

questions.question: Do you want to download the statement as a PDF or a CSV file?
questions.why: The portal offers both a 'View statement' option (which leads to a PDF) and a direct 'Download CSV' button for each pay period.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose a spreadsheet format (CSV) over a visual document format (PDF) for their financial records.
questions.verify_form: Both a PDF and a CSV were on offer - check which the agent took; whether your records need a document or a spreadsheet is your call.

questions.question: Which type of document do you want to download for this order?
questions.why: The download prompt requires choosing between a standard invoice and a warranty document that includes the IMEI number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify whether you need the standard receipt or the detailed warranty information for your records.
questions.verify_form: Two document types were offered - the plain invoice and the warranty slip with the IMEI; which one your records need is your call - check which was fetched.

questions.question: Should you download these statements individually or use the checkboxes to batch export them into a single combined file?
questions.why: The interface provides checkboxes next to each statement and a 'Download selected' button, giving you the choice between managing multiple individual files or one consolidated document.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to dictate how your records are organized, potentially ending up with a cluttered folder of individual files instead of one neat, combined PDF.
questions.verify_form: Checkboxes allowed one combined download - check whether the agent fetched one merged file or many singles; how your records are organized is your preference.

questions.question: Where do you want to save the PDF, and should I create a new folder for it?
questions.why: The Files app save interface presents multiple existing folders like 'Downloads' and 'Documents', along with an option to create a new folder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to organize the downloaded file into a specific or newly created folder of their choice.
questions.verify_form: The save dialog offered folders and a new-folder option - check where the agent put the file and whether that is where you will look for it.

questions.question: Do you want to rename this PDF receipt before saving it, or keep the default generated filename?
questions.why: The system 'Save As' dialog defaults to a random string of characters that does not describe the receipt.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to assign a recognizable name to the file, potentially making it harder to find later.
questions.verify_form: The proposed filename is a meaningless string - the agent decided whether to keep it; check you can still find and recognize the file later.

questions.question: Are you okay with saving the file as 'MyMountSinai - Test Details' in the 'Test' folder?
questions.why: The save dialog proposes a specific file name and destination folder, which dictates how easily you will be able to find the document later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to rename the file to something more meaningful or select a specific folder for better organization.
questions.verify_form: The dialog proposed a name and folder - the agent accepted them; check the file landed where you expect under a name you recognize.

questions.question: Where and with what name should you save the video file?
questions.why: The Save As dialog prompts for a filename and location, showing a default alphanumeric name and the Desktop folder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose a recognizable filename and a specific folder location for the downloaded file.
questions.verify_form: The save dialog asked for a name and location - check both; a token filename on the desktop is what you get by default.

questions.question: Did the file open directly in a new browser tab instead of triggering a local download?
questions.why: Browsers often render PDFs natively instead of downloading them, requiring a secondary action (like clicking the browser's save icon) to actually store the file locally.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that the file is only temporarily cached in the browser rather than permanently saved to their device.

questions.question: Did a brief 'Preparing download' toast notification appear and vanish on the page?
questions.why: Many portals show a transient visual message while generating a file. A sighted user sees this and knows to wait, but it disappears too quickly for a later check.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate, transient confirmation that the site is actively processing the request, potentially leading to confusion if the browser download doesn't start instantly.

questions.question: How is the download progressing, and what should you do while it finishes?
questions.why: The Chrome download bar shows the file is only partially downloaded with 35 seconds remaining, meaning you must decide whether to wait or proactively open the destination folder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to monitor the real-time download speed and proactively prepare the destination folder before the file finishes arriving.

questions.question: Did the download complete successfully, or did the browser report a network error that requires you to resume it?
questions.why: Large files or unstable connections can cause a download to fail midway, meaning you must check the download manager for an error state and manually trigger a retry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might see that the download started and assume it will finish, missing the silent network failure that requires intervention.

questions.question: How do you locate the downloaded archive on your local file system?
questions.why: Clicking the folder icon next to the most recent 354 KB zip file ensures you can access the actual file on your computer rather than just seeing its status in the browser.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate, visual confirmation of exactly which local folder the file was saved to.

questions.question: Has the file fully finished downloading into your local Downloads folder?
questions.why: The file explorer currently shows a '.crdownload' file, indicating that the download is still in progress and the file is not yet ready to use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually confirm in your local file system that the temporary download file has successfully converted into the final, usable document.

questions.question: Does the browser's download surface show the expected file arrived - the right name and a plausible size - before you rely on it?
questions.why: The screen shows a download status bar at the bottom, indicating the file has arrived.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to confirm the correct file was downloaded and is accessible.

questions.question: Is the correct file shown as successfully downloaded in the browser's downloads menu?
questions.why: Checking the Safari downloads menu confirms that the specific file, such as the 21 KB Notice of Assessment PDF, actually arrived on your device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the immediate visual confirmation that the exact file you need was successfully saved to your local machine.

questions.question: Before leaving the site, does the browser show the download actually triggered - an entry in the downloads UI rather than just the page you were on?
questions.why: The screen displays the article abstract page, requiring you to confirm the download triggered successfully before returning to the desktop.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to manually verify the file's arrival in their local environment before the browser session ends.

questions.question: If the file isn't in your standard downloads folder, did the browser silently save it to the last used directory instead?
questions.why: Browsers often default to the last directory you saved a file to, so if it's missing from your expected folder, you must check the browser's download manager to find its actual location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might fail the task assuming the download didn't happen, rather than using the browser's history to locate the misrouted file.

questions.question: Do you approve the final payment amount, including the added processing fee?
questions.why: The payment portal adds a ₦4,500.00 processing fee to the original ₦300,000.00 invoice total, changing the final amount required to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review and authorize unexpected surcharges before your funds are committed.
questions.verify_form: A processing fee was added on top of the invoice total - the agent was at a payment step; check no money moved without you approving the new amount.

questions.question: Did you open the downloaded file to verify its contents are correct?
questions.why: Opening the 6-page PDF statement in the Files app confirms that the correct file was downloaded and saved properly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the direct confirmation that the downloaded file contains the expected information and is not corrupted or incorrect.

questions.question: Does the downloaded file match the specific form you set out to find?
questions.why: The title screen promises to show how to get a W2 tax form, which matches the blank 2021 W-2 Wage and Tax Statement PDF accessed later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent downloads the wrong file, you will not have the correct document for your administrative needs.

questions.question: Did you scroll past the initial notice to verify the actual tax form loaded?
questions.why: The first page only displayed an 'Attention' notice, making it necessary to check the second page to confirm the actual Form 1098 was present.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance that the correct document was retrieved rather than just a generic cover sheet or an incomplete file.

questions.question: Which application should you use to open the downloaded file?
questions.why: The system dialog presents multiple personal and work applications like Drive PDF Viewer and Mi PDF Viewer to open the document.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose your preferred PDF viewer and decide whether to make it the default application.
questions.verify_form: An open-with chooser appeared - check which app the agent picked and whether it set a default; that choice sticks to future files.

questions.question: Do you see all the selected invoices combined in the downloaded PDF?
questions.why: Scrolling through the document revealed multiple distinct invoices like 'Invoice No. 331' and 'Invoice No. 338', confirming the multi-voucher export succeeded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual confirmation that the downloaded file actually contains all the requested invoices rather than just a single one.

questions.question: Has the file finished downloading, and how do you open it?
questions.why: The browser's download bar displays 'onlineStatement.pdf' as completed, confirming the file is ready to be viewed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to immediately open and visually verify that the downloaded file contains the correct information.

questions.question: Does the saved PDF display the required account balance, account number, and source URL?
questions.why: Confirming the document shows the $1,600.00 balance, account ending in *4436, and the BMO Harris URL ensures it serves as valid proof even without a name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of manually verifying that the downloaded file contains the exact financial and source details required for your records.

questions.question: Does the generated PDF receipt contain all the correct information?
questions.why: The screen displays the contents of 'SalesReceipt-4.pdf', including specific billing details, item descriptions, and tax amounts that must be checked for accuracy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally verify that the downloaded receipt contains the correct invoice details and amounts.

questions.question: Is the presentation displaying correctly and what are the prerequisites?
questions.why: The screen shows the opened CS101 PowerPoint presentation, confirming the file was successfully downloaded and can be viewed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the direct confirmation that the file opens properly and the audio instructions regarding required software.

questions.question: Does the downloaded PDF contain the correct statement details?
questions.why: Reviewing the ANZ logo, statement dates, and transaction totals confirms that the correct document was successfully downloaded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the downloaded file contains the correct financial records.

questions.question: Is the downloaded file's extension actually a document format like PDF, rather than an executable or script?
questions.why: Malicious sites often serve executable files disguised as documents, and checking the file extension before opening it is a critical security step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the critical security check of verifying the file type, risking executing malware on their machine.

questions.question: Did the system silently fail by generating a blank PDF instead of your populated tax form?
questions.why: Opening the generated 1098-T PDF reveals a completely blank document, which is the system's silent failure mode when your Social Security Number is missing from your profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual realization that the downloaded file is empty, which is the critical trigger to realize you must go update your SSN before the form can be generated properly.

questions.question: Does the downloaded document clearly indicate that the invoice has been paid?
questions.why: Opening the PDF reveals a large green 'PAID' watermark across the center, which serves as the official visual proof of payment for the client.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that the downloaded file is actually a finalized receipt rather than just a copy of the original unpaid invoice.

questions.question: Did the browser download an HTML login page instead of the actual PDF?
questions.why: If your session expired or you lack access rights, the site might silently redirect the download link to a login page, resulting in a downloaded file that is just HTML rather than your document.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might see a successful file download and stop, handing over a useless login page instead of the requested academic paper or bank statement.

questions.question: Does the downloaded file display the correct application icon in the file explorer?
questions.why: A file saved as a PDF might actually be an HTML login page if the session expired, which is often immediately obvious because the OS assigns a generic or browser icon instead of the PDF reader icon.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the quick visual heuristic that the downloaded file is actually the expected document format rather than an error page.

questions.question: Does the file size of the downloaded document indicate a successful export, or is it suspiciously small?
questions.why: The browser's download manager displays the final file size, and a very small file (like 1 KB) often means the site exported an error page or an empty archive instead of the actual data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might blindly hand over a corrupted or empty file, leaving you without the actual document you requested.

questions.question: How should you extract the downloaded file to access its contents?
questions.why: The context menu offers multiple extraction options like WinRAR, and extracting to a dedicated folder keeps the downloaded contents organized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose your preferred extraction utility and folder structure for organizing the downloaded files.
questions.verify_form: The archive needed an extractor and a destination - check what unpacked it and where; a scattered extraction is hard to clean up.

questions.question: Does the extracted archive contain all the expected product folders and files?
questions.why: Opening folders like 'Fit' and 'Gemini' confirms that the downloaded archive successfully captured the specific data you requested.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your specific personal data, like your Fit activities or Gemini history, was actually included in the export.

questions.question: Where should you move the downloaded file for safekeeping?
questions.why: The screen shows a file being copied from the Downloads folder to a specific folder on an external drive, indicating a need to store the file in a designated backup location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the file is organized into their preferred personal storage hierarchy rather than just left in the default downloads folder.
questions.verify_form: The file sits in Downloads - the agent decided whether to move it; check it reached the folder or drive where you actually keep these.

questions.question: Who are you sending this email to, and is the correct PDF attached?
questions.why: The screen shows an email draft with an Amazon order PDF attached, so you must ensure the recipient address is correct before sending sensitive purchase information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally confirm the recipient's email address, risking the accidental disclosure of your private order receipt to the wrong person.
questions.verify_form: The document is attached to an outgoing email - check the recipient address yourself before anything sends; a receipt to the wrong person cannot be recalled.

questions.question: How do you confirm the logout prompt to securely end your session?
questions.why: The screen displays a confirmation dialog asking if you want to log out, which requires clicking the confirm button to actually end the session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their account was securely closed after handling sensitive downloaded documents.
